footer.aboutTitle: About This Train Driver Entrance Exam
footer.topicText: This fictional aptitude challenge uses display-board reading, timing, route logic, observation, sequencing, and prioritisation to create a fun staged test.
footer.aboutText: This quiz is for entertainment and self-challenge only. It is not an official railway recruitment test, train-driver licence assessment, training programme, operating manual, or professional qualification. Every rule needed to answer is stated inside the question.

stageGroups.title: Platform Focus
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. The next round asks you to read the details more carefully.

questions.prompt: A board says: Platform 2 - Lakeside. Platform 3 - Hilltown. You need Hilltown. Which platform do you choose?
questions.explanation: Hilltown is listed beside Platform 3.

questions.prompt: A route card lists a ticket, map, water, and pen. Which item is missing from: ticket, map, pen?
questions.explanation: Water is the only listed item missing.

questions.prompt: A sign says the blue exit is east and the red exit is south. If you face east, which exit is on your right?
questions.explanation: When you face east, south is on your right, so the red exit is on your right.

questions.prompt: A display originally reads 14:10. It is changed to 14:40. What changed?
questions.explanation: Only the time has changed.

questions.prompt: Four markers are shown: circle, square, triangle, circle. Which shape appears twice?
questions.explanation: Circle appears first and fourth.

questions.prompt: The map shows three adjacent locations in this order: Gate A, lift, café. Which location is directly beside the café?
questions.explanation: In the stated order, the lift is immediately before and directly beside the café.

questions.prompt: A notice says: use Platform 1 only after 09:00. It is 08:55. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: 09:00 is five minutes away.

stageGroups.title: Display Board Details
stageGroups.encouragement: The boards are getting busier. Keep the important clues in view.

questions.prompt: Board A says: Coastline 11:20, Platform 5. Board B says: Coastline 11:35, Platform 5. What differs?
questions.explanation: The destination and platform match; the time differs.

questions.prompt: A route board lists Northbay, Elm Park, Rivergate. A second board lists Northbay, Rivergate. Which stop is missing from the second board?
questions.explanation: Elm Park appears only on the first board.

questions.prompt: A notice says: a blue marker identifies the quiet route. Which marker identifies the quiet route?
questions.explanation: The notice explicitly assigns blue to the quiet route.

questions.prompt: A board shows Route A: Pine, Lake, Market. Which route matches the board?
questions.explanation: Only the first option keeps the stated order.

questions.prompt: A board says 16:05 and a handwritten update says delayed by 10 minutes. What is the new time?
questions.explanation: Adding 10 minutes to 16:05 gives 16:15.

questions.prompt: A display uses a star beside services with bicycle space. Which service has bicycle space?
questions.explanation: The legend defines the star symbol.

questions.prompt: A route card says: Marker 7, then Marker 9, then Marker 12. Which marker comes immediately after Marker 7?
questions.explanation: Marker 9 follows Marker 7 on the card.

stageGroups.title: Timetable Timing
stageGroups.encouragement: Good timing. Next, you will need to map the route as well as read it.

questions.prompt: A train leaves at 09:15 and arrives at 09:50. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: From 09:15 to 09:50 is 35 minutes.

questions.prompt: A service due at 12:40 is delayed by 15 minutes. When is it now due?
questions.explanation: 12:40 plus 15 minutes is 12:55.

questions.prompt: It is 17:20. A train leaves at 17:45. How much time remains?
questions.explanation: There are 25 minutes between 17:20 and 17:45.

questions.prompt: Train A leaves at 08:50. Train B leaves at 09:05. Which leaves first?
questions.explanation: 08:50 is earlier than 09:05.

questions.prompt: A journey takes 40 minutes. It starts at 13:25. When does it finish?
questions.explanation: 13:25 plus 40 minutes is 14:05.

questions.prompt: A board shows 10:30, 10:50, and 11:10. What is the gap between each service?
questions.explanation: Each listed time is 20 minutes later.

questions.prompt: A 14:00 departure is moved 20 minutes earlier. What is the new departure time?
questions.explanation: Twenty minutes before 14:00 is 13:40.

stageGroups.title: Route Finder
stageGroups.encouragement: The route is changing. The next round introduces the signal rules.

questions.prompt: On a grid, the depot is one square north of the station. Which move reaches the depot from the station?
questions.explanation: The depot is stated to be north of the station.

questions.prompt: Route A has 3 stops and avoids Platform 4. Route B has 5 stops and passes through blocked Platform 4. Which route both has fewer stops and avoids the blocked platform?
questions.explanation: Route A has fewer stops and is explicitly stated to avoid blocked Platform 4.

questions.prompt: A route instruction says: go east, then north. Where are you relative to the start?
questions.explanation: East followed by north ends north-east of the start.

questions.prompt: A map shows Platform 4 is delayed. Which platform has the delay?
questions.explanation: The map explicitly identifies Platform 4.

questions.prompt: Platforms 1, 2, and 3 are open; Platform 4 is blocked. Route X uses Platforms 2 then 3, while Route Y uses Platform 4. Which route is available?
questions.explanation: Route X uses only open Platforms 2 and 3; Route Y uses blocked Platform 4.

questions.prompt: From the station, the museum is west and the park is east. Which place is east of the station?
questions.explanation: The map places the park east of the station.

questions.prompt: A route card says: Start, Bridge, Tunnel, End. Which location is between Bridge and End?
questions.explanation: Tunnel is listed between Bridge and End.

stageGroups.title: Signal Clues
stageGroups.encouragement: The rules now need to be followed in the right order.

questions.prompt: Fictional rules: amber means wait; white means confirmed. A route has a white card, but an amber marker is showing. Marker instructions come before route status. What happens first?
questions.explanation: The amber instruction comes first, so the team waits even though the route has a white confirmation card.

questions.prompt: A double bell means check the display board first. The board says Platform 2, while the route card says Platform 5. Which action follows the bell rule?
questions.explanation: The double-bell rule requires the display board to be checked before either platform is chosen.

questions.prompt: Fictional rules: Signal A means continue to the listed route; Signal B means wait for confirmation. Signal B appears while a shorter route is offered. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting for confirmation, regardless of the shorter route.

questions.prompt: A white card means confirmed, and only confirmed routes may be selected. Route A has a white card; Route B has an amber card. Which route can be selected?
questions.explanation: Only Route A has the white confirmation card required by the selection rule.

questions.prompt: A notice says: if the display and route card disagree, verify the display before choosing. The display says Platform 2 and the route card says Platform 3. What should you do first?
questions.explanation: The stated rule requires checking the display before choosing between the two platforms.

questions.prompt: Green means open and amber means wait. Route C has 4 stops with a green marker; Route D has 2 stops with amber. Rule: select an open route even when it is longer. Which route fits?
questions.explanation: Route C is marked open; Route D requires waiting despite having fewer stops.

questions.prompt: A red marker means read the attached note before choosing. The note changes the platform from 3 to 6. Which action must occur before Platform 6 can be chosen?
questions.explanation: The red-marker rule requires the note to be read before its Platform 6 update is used.

stageGroups.title: Sequence Checks
stageGroups.encouragement: You have the rules. Next, see how well you retain the earlier details.

questions.prompt: Checklist: read the board, check the route card, then choose a platform. The board and route card have both been checked and now agree on Platform 3. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The first two checks are complete, so the final checklist step is choosing the agreed Platform 3.

questions.prompt: Rule: verify the time before comparing platforms. The time has been verified as 13:20, but Platforms 2 and 5 have not been compared. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Time verification is complete, so platform comparison is the next stated step.

questions.prompt: Three checks must satisfy both rules: the board before the route card, and the route card before the marker. Which order works?
questions.explanation: Board, card, marker is the only order that satisfies both stated dependencies.

questions.prompt: Rule: check uncertain details before acting. The time is confirmed, but the platform number is uncertain. Which step must occur before the route is chosen?
questions.explanation: The platform is the only uncertain detail, so it must be checked before choosing the route.

questions.prompt: A board update must be read after the bell and before the route card. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: The board sits between the bell and route card.

questions.prompt: A process says: confirm the marker, confirm the time, then choose. The marker has been confirmed, but the time has not. What must happen next?
questions.explanation: The marker check is complete, so the next required step is confirming the time.

questions.prompt: A notice says a change is checked before a schedule is shared. The schedule says 14:00, but the change is not checked yet. Which action comes later?
questions.explanation: The stated order puts checking the change before sharing the schedule.

stageGroups.title: Observation Desk
stageGroups.encouragement: You remembered the details. Now prioritise them under pressure.

questions.prompt: Earlier, a blue marker identified which route?
questions.explanation: The earlier display-board rule defined blue as the quiet route.

questions.prompt: Card A says Platform 2, 10:20. Card B says Platform 2, 10:50. What is different?
questions.explanation: Both cards name Platform 2, but their times differ.

questions.prompt: Board A lists Oak, Pine, Lake, Hill. Board B lists Oak, Pine, Hill. Which stop appears only on Board A?
questions.explanation: Lake is the only stop present on Board A and absent from Board B.

questions.prompt: Card A says Gate C, 16:20, Northbay. Card B says Gate D, 16:20, Northbay. Which detail differs?
questions.explanation: The time and destination match; only the gate changes from C to D.

questions.prompt: Notice A says Riverline, 18:10, Platform 1. Notice B says Coastline, 18:10, Platform 6. Which detail matches?
questions.explanation: Both notices show 18:10, while their routes and platforms differ.

questions.prompt: A board says: Oak, Pine, Elm. A card says: Oak, Elm, Pine. Which item moved?
questions.explanation: Pine and Elm appear in the opposite order.

questions.prompt: The board reads Circle 7, Square 9, Triangle 4. The route card reads Circle 7, Square 6, Triangle 4. Which symbol has the mismatched number?
questions.explanation: Square is paired with 9 on the board and 6 on the route card; the other pairs match.

stageGroups.title: Priority Rules
stageGroups.encouragement: The final rounds combine the clues rather than showing them one at a time.

questions.prompt: Rule: safety confirmation comes before speed. One route is faster, but its platform detail is unconfirmed. What has priority?
questions.explanation: The stated rule puts confirmation before speed.

questions.prompt: Earlier, Platform 4 was delayed. Before directing a passenger group there, what should you check first?
questions.explanation: The known delay makes the current platform status the relevant first check.

questions.prompt: Rule: when two updates conflict, verify the uncertain detail before sharing either one. Update A says 14:10; Update B says 14:40 and has an unreadable source label. What should happen first?
questions.explanation: Update B contains the uncertain source detail, so that source must be verified before either time is shared.

questions.prompt: A board is confirmed, but a handwritten note is unclear. Rule: confirmed information outranks unclear information until the note is checked. Which should guide the next choice?
questions.explanation: The stated framework prioritises confirmed information.

questions.prompt: Rule: if a route is blocked, do not select it even if it is shorter. Route A is blocked and Route B is open. Which route can be selected?
questions.explanation: Only the open route meets the rule.

questions.prompt: Rule: check missing details before finalising. Route A has a confirmed time but no platform; Route B has both details confirmed. What must happen before Route A can be finalised?
questions.explanation: Route A is missing its platform, so that detail must be checked before Route A can be finalised.

questions.prompt: Priority rule: confirmed information outranks preference. Route A is preferred but unconfirmed; Route B is confirmed and open. Which route has priority?
questions.explanation: Route B has priority because it is confirmed and open, while Route A is only preferred.

stageGroups.title: Calm Decisions
stageGroups.encouragement: One final synthesis round remains. Keep every stated clue in view.

questions.prompt: Two updates arrive: the display says 15:30, while the route card has no time. Rule: verify missing details before acting. What should you verify?
questions.explanation: The route card is missing the relevant time detail.

questions.prompt: The display says Platform 2 at 16:10; the route card says Platform 5 at 16:10. Rule: verify the display before choosing when platforms conflict. What is the next step?
questions.explanation: The times match but the platforms conflict, so the stated rule requires the display to be verified.

questions.prompt: Earlier, Signal B meant wait for confirmation. Signal B is showing and a new route looks shorter. What should happen first?
questions.explanation: The Signal B rule still applies before choosing a route.

questions.prompt: A route card says Platform 6; the board marks Platform 6 delayed. Rule: check a known delay before using that platform. Which detail should be checked?
questions.explanation: Platform 6 has the known delay, so its current status is the relevant detail to check.

questions.prompt: Two routes are open. Route A has a confirmed time; Route B has an unconfirmed time. Rule: confirmed details outrank unconfirmed details. Which route has the stronger basis?
questions.explanation: Route A has the confirmed time.

questions.prompt: Route A has a confirmed time but its platform is missing. Route B has both details but is marked closed. Rule: never guess missing details or use a closed route. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Route B cannot be used because it is closed, while Route A becomes usable only after its missing platform is verified.

questions.prompt: The board shows Platform 3, but its destination is unreadable. The route card shows Platform 3 and Northbay. Rule: verify unclear board details before acting. What comes first?
questions.explanation: The platform matches, but the board destination is unclear and must be verified under the stated rule.

questions.prompt: A train leaves at 10:20 and the route card says the journey takes 25 minutes. What arrival time matches both clues?
questions.explanation: 10:20 plus 25 minutes is 10:45.

questions.prompt: A blue marker means quiet route. The blue route has 3 stops; the red route has 5. Which option is both quiet and shorter?
questions.explanation: Blue identifies the quiet route, and three stops are fewer than five.

questions.prompt: Signal B means wait for confirmation. A board and route card disagree about a platform, and the rule says verify the display before choosing. Which complete sequence follows both rules?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting for confirmation; the conflict rule then requires display verification before a platform is chosen.

questions.prompt: Platform 4 is delayed. A board lists Platform 4 at 11:10 and Platform 2 at 11:20. Rule: check a known delay before choosing. Which detail matters first?
questions.explanation: The current Platform 4 delay is the stated uncertainty that must be checked before comparing the options.

questions.prompt: A route instruction says east then north. A display says the destination is north-east of the station. Do the instruction and display agree?
questions.explanation: Moving east then north ends north-east of the start.

questions.prompt: Checklist: check the time, check the marker, then choose. The time is confirmed and the marker is blue, meaning quiet route. Which action completes the checklist?
questions.explanation: Both checks are complete, and the blue marker identifies the quiet route to choose.

questions.prompt: Rules: blue marks the quiet route; Platform 4 is delayed; Signal B means wait for confirmation. Signal B is showing, and the board offers blue-marked Platform 2 or delayed Platform 4. Which sequence uses all three clues?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting first. Platform 4's delay is then checked, and the blue marker identifies Platform 2 as the quiet choice.
